Location: Lakeview Retreat Center, Dundas, MN
Facilitator: R. Lindqvist (external)

The retreat was attended by all six directors, the executive director, and the office manager.

amendment.

The NLAC charter describes the service region as a six-county area. Record status: current.

The discussion on the service region was lengthy. The current charter describes the service
region as a six-county area. Several directors noted that the northern counties have seen
significant population growth and that demand for services in those counties is rising. The
executive director presented intake data showing that 28% of new cases in the last fiscal year
originated in the two northernmost counties of the region.

T. Ellison and seconded by M. O'Dell. After debate, the motion failed on a 3-3 vote. Those in
favor cited the intake data and the need to be responsive to unmet need. Those opposed cited
the current staffing constraints and the risk of diluting services in the existing region. The
board agreed to revisit the question at the annual meeting in the fall, with a request that the
executive director prepare a more detailed capacity analysis.

Other retreat outcomes:
- The board affirmed the current mission statement and the priority of family law and housing
  matters.
- The board asked the fundraising committee to develop a three-year development plan.
- The board requested a facilities condition report for the October meeting.

Facilitator's note: The executive director requested that the retreat notes be circulated to
staff; the board agreed.

**Northfield Legal Aid Collaborative**
**Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2023–2024**
**Submitted to the Board of Directors, September 2024**

---

**A MESSAGE FROM THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**

This year marked our twenty-sixth year of service to the Northfield community. When we opened our doors in 1998 with a single staff attorney and a borrowed conference room at St. Anne's Parish, we could not have imagined the scope of need we would come to address. This annual report reflects a year of significant growth, a renewed commitment to our founding values, and a clear-eyed look at the challenges that lie ahead.

I want to thank our staff, our volunteer attorneys, our pro bono partners, and our funders. The work described in these pages is only possible through collective effort. We enter the coming year with a strategic plan that will guide us toward greater impact, deeper community partnerships, and a more sustainable organization.

Sincerely,

*Marilyn Voss*
Executive Director

---

**MISSION & VISION**

**Mission:** To provide high-quality, free civil legal services to low-income residents of Northfield County, ensuring equal access to justice regardless of income.

**Vision:** A community where all residents have the legal representation and counsel they need to secure stable housing, safe families, and economic security.

**Core Values:**
- **Client-Centered Service:** We listen first, and we measure our success by the outcomes our clients achieve.
- **Community Partnership:** We work alongside other organizations to address the root causes of poverty and injustice.
- **Equity & Inclusion:** We strive to make our services accessible to all, and we work to dismantle barriers that have historically excluded marginalized communities.
- **Stewardship:** We use our resources carefully, honoring the trust placed in us by our funders and the public.

---

**HIGHLIGHTS OF THE YEAR**

- **Cases Opened:** 403 new cases were opened, a 12% increase over the prior fiscal year.
- **Cases Closed:** 371 cases were closed, with a 70% success rate (full relief, partial relief, or negotiated settlement).
- **New Evening Clinic:** The evening clinic pilot, launched in January, met its target attendance of 5–8 clients per session, averaging 6 clients per session over the quarter. This success has led us to plan for a permanent expansion of evening hours.
- **Pro Bono Network:** 34 volunteer attorneys logged 412 hours, and our volunteer clinics served 89 clients.
- **New Staff Positions:** We added a full-time Staff Attorney for Housing and a part-time Bilingual Intake Coordinator, funded in part by a two-year grant from the Meyer Family Foundation.

---

**PROGRAM AREAS**

**Housing Stability Program**

Housing remains our largest practice area, reflecting the ongoing crisis in Northfield. This year, we opened 158 housing cases, including eviction defense, habitability claims, and foreclosure prevention. Eviction filings in the downtown corridor continue to rise, driven largely by rent increases. We have also seen an increase in habitability complaints from tenants in older buildings, a trend we expect to continue into the fall.

Our housing attorneys have secured full or partial relief in 62% of closed housing cases. We have expanded our partnerships with the Northfield Housing Authority and the Tenant Union to provide on-site intake at their offices twice a month.

**Family Law Program**

We opened 87 family law cases this year, covering custody, divorce, and protective orders. Our family law practice remains a critical service for survivors of domestic violence, many of whom are referred to us by the Harbor House shelter. We continue to offer a weekly clinic for protective order filings, staffed by a volunteer attorney and a legal advocate.

ARTICLE I — OFFICES
Section 1. Principal Office. The principal office shall be at 214 Division Street South, Northfield, MN. The board may change the principal office upon ten (10) days' written notice to all directors.

Section 2. Other Offices. The corporation may also have offices at such other places as the board may from time to time determine.

ARTICLE II — PURPOSE
The purpose of the Collaborative shall be as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. The Collaborative shall not engage in any activities not permitted by Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.

ARTICLE III — BOARD OF DIRECTORS
Section 1. Powers. The board shall manage the affairs of the corporation and may exercise all powers of the corporation, except those expressly reserved to the members by law or these Bylaws.

Section 2. Composition. The board shall consist of not fewer than five (5) and not more than fifteen (15) directors. Directors need not be residents of Minnesota.

Section 3. Initial Directors. The initial directors shall serve until the first annual meeting of the board, or until their successors are elected and qualified. The initial directors are:

Northfield Legal Aid Collaborative founded year 1998 year. Record status: current.

Section 4. Terms. Directors shall serve staggered two-year terms. At the first annual meeting, three directors shall be elected to two-year terms and three to one-year terms, as determined by lot.

Section 5. Meetings. Regular meetings shall be held quarterly. Special meetings may be called by the President or by any three directors upon five (5) days' notice. Meetings shall be held at the principal office unless otherwise specified.

Section 6. Quorum. A majority of directors then in office shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business.

ARTICLE IV — OFFICERS
Section 1. Officers. The officers of the corporation shall be a President, a Vice President, a Secretary, and a Treasurer. Any two offices may be held by the same person, except President and Secretary.

Section 2. Duties. The President shall preside at all meetings of the board. The Vice President shall perform the duties of the President in the President's absence. The Secretary shall keep minutes, give notices, and have custody of corporate records. The Treasurer shall have custody of corporate funds and securities, and shall keep full and accurate accounts.

ARTICLE V — COMMITTEES
The board may create standing or ad hoc committees. Each committee shall have a written charge and shall report to the board at each regular meeting.

ARTICLE VI — CONTRACTS AND LOANS
Section 1. Contracts. The board may authorize any officer or agent to enter into contracts on behalf of the corporation.

Section 2. Loans. No loans shall be contracted on behalf of the corporation without board approval by two-thirds vote of directors present.

ARTICLE VII — INDEMNIFICATION
The corporation shall indemnify any person who was or is a party to any proceeding by reason of the fact that they are or were a director or officer, to the fullest extent permitted by Minnesota law.

BOARD RETREAT NOTES — FACILITATOR'S SUMMARY

Date: June 11-12, 2005
Location: Lakeview Retreat Center, Dundas, MN
Facilitator: R. Lindqvist (external)

The retreat was attended by all six directors, the executive director, and the office manager.
The purpose was to review the strategic plan and to consider the possible service region
amendment.

The NLAC charter describes the service region as a six-county area. Record status: current.

The discussion on the service region was lengthy. The current charter describes the service
region as a six-county area. Several directors noted that the northern counties have seen
significant population growth and that demand for services in those counties is rising. The
executive director presented intake data showing that 28% of new cases in the last fiscal year
originated in the two northernmost counties of the region.

A motion to pursue a charter amendment to expand the region to eight counties was made by
T. Ellison and seconded by M. O'Dell. After debate, the motion failed on a 3-3 vote. Those in
favor cited the intake data and the need to be responsive to unmet need. Those opposed cited
the current staffing constraints and the risk of diluting services in the existing region. The
board agreed to revisit the question at the annual meeting in the fall, with a request that the
executive director prepare a more detailed capacity analysis.

Other retreat outcomes:
- The board affirmed the current mission statement and the priority of family law and housing
  matters.
- The board asked the fundraising committee to develop a three-year development plan.
- The board requested a facilities condition report for the October meeting.

**Northfield Legal Aid Collaborative**
**Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2023–2024**
**Submitted to the Board of Directors, September 2024**

---

**A MESSAGE FROM THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**

This year marked our twenty-sixth year of service to the Northfield community. When we opened our doors in 1998 with a single staff attorney and a borrowed conference room at St. Anne's Parish, we could not have imagined the scope of need we would come to address. This annual report reflects a year of significant growth, a renewed commitment to our founding values, and a clear-eyed look at the challenges that lie ahead.

I want to thank our staff, our volunteer attorneys, our pro bono partners, and our funders. The work described in these pages is only possible through collective effort. We enter the coming year with a strategic plan that will guide us toward greater impact, deeper community partnerships, and a more sustainable organization.

Sincerely,

*Marilyn Voss*
Executive Director

---

**MISSION & VISION**

**Mission:** To provide high-quality, free civil legal services to low-income residents of Northfield County, ensuring equal access to justice regardless of income.

**Vision:** A community where all residents have the legal representation and counsel they need to secure stable housing, safe families, and economic security.

**Core Values:**
- **Client-Centered Service:** We listen first, and we measure our success by the outcomes our clients achieve.
- **Community Partnership:** We work alongside other organizations to address the root causes of poverty and injustice.
- **Equity & Inclusion:** We strive to make our services accessible to all, and we work to dismantle barriers that have historically excluded marginalized communities.
- **Stewardship:** We use our resources carefully, honoring the trust placed in us by our funders and the public.

---

**HIGHLIGHTS OF THE YEAR**

- **Cases Opened:** 403 new cases were opened, a 12% increase over the prior fiscal year.
- **Cases Closed:** 371 cases were closed, with a 70% success rate (full relief, partial relief, or negotiated settlement).
- **New Evening Clinic:** The evening clinic pilot, launched in January, met its target attendance of 5–8 clients per session, averaging 6 clients per session over the quarter. This success has led us to plan for a permanent expansion of evening hours.
- **Pro Bono Network:** 34 volunteer attorneys logged 412 hours, and our volunteer clinics served 89 clients.
- **New Staff Positions:** We added a full-time Staff Attorney for Housing and a part-time Bilingual Intake Coordinator, funded in part by a two-year grant from the Meyer Family Foundation.

---

**PROGRAM AREAS**

**Housing Stability Program**

Housing remains our largest practice area, reflecting the ongoing crisis in Northfield. This year, we opened 158 housing cases, including eviction defense, habitability claims, and foreclosure prevention. Eviction filings in the downtown corridor continue to rise, driven largely by rent increases. We have also seen an increase in habitability complaints from tenants in older buildings, a trend we expect to continue into the fall.

Our housing attorneys have secured full or partial relief in 62% of closed housing cases. We have expanded our partnerships with the Northfield Housing Authority and the Tenant Union to provide on-site intake at their offices twice a month.

**Family Law Program**

We opened 87 family law cases this year, covering custody, divorce, and protective orders. Our family law practice remains a critical service for survivors of domestic violence, many of whom are referred to us by the Harbor House shelter. We continue to offer a weekly clinic for protective order filings, staffed by a volunteer attorney and a legal advocate.
